The second has:

  • some semblance of a storyline
  • monster infighting (though this can be easily missed, levels become less enemy-packed as the game goes on)
  • lots of cutting edge engine features at the time (e.g.: dinos' limbs are modeled separately, and they have separate hurt animations for each limb; enemies no longer respawn on a timer [a notable feat considering the level sizes], and only some of the original enemies respawn when you reenter a level, etc.)
  • the game is MUCH larger, and (IMO) much more punishing as the game progresses. It doesn't feel unfair though, because you have....
  • creatively absurd weapons. The first had tons of weapons, many of which were redundant/generic beyond reason. All of the weapons in the second serve a specific purpose and are doubleplusgood in certain situations. E.g. Cerebral bore, which one-shots enemies that have a discernible head and can lock through walls; Scorpion launcher, which fires three missiles that can launch and track three separate enemies at once. You get the idea.
  • There is a fear system, and boy is it satisfying. Early on, everyone wants a piece of you. However, replay an early level with an broken late-game weapon and the dinos will run when they see you - arms flailing and everything.
